“What are you talking about, Sarah?{r}{p}I love you.{r}{p}Why would I try to kill you?!{r}{P}”
Robert spoke as if hurt, spread his arms, and tried to step toward me.
“...I've figured it all out.{r}{p}Who knew I was going to Eddie Bauer's place on Tuesday night?{r}{p}You did.”
“Who could tamper with Kaminski's car?{r}{P}{p}Who could shoot the cautious Lieutenant Nolte dead from the front?{r}{P}{p}It was easy for you, his colleague.”
I shook my head as I spoke.
Robert was silent for a while, then began to speak in a voice like a different man's.
“...It started with something trivial.{r}{p}You know how it goes, don't you?{r}{P}

“The Organization.{r}{p}At first they just buy you a drink now and then.{r}{p}Before long the bar becomes a club, you start accepting little gifts...{p}and when you realize it, you're leaking information about the raids.”
“A pampered girl like you will never understand in your whole life!{r}{P}”
It was the first time I'd heard such hatred in Robert's voice, and it felt like a stake driven into my chest.
You killed so many of my dear friends...”
At my words, Robert twisted his lips into a smile.
No thanks.{r}{p}I've got a car waiting out back.
And all the money I've saved.
Enough to live it up for life somewhere like Mexico.{r}{p}...Sarah,
Too bad.{r}{p}I really did love you.{r}{p}...Sorry, but I'm leaving.”
I steadied my aim again, but my welling tears blurred Robert's figure.
Toward Robert's back, warped by my tears, I squeezed the trigger...

{n1} and I nodded and leaned forward.

I stepped on {n1}'s foot as he started to say it.
“Even if you've heard a similar story a few times, the details may differ, so discard any prior knowledge.{r}{p}Understood?”
“Please explain the relationships around the victim.”
The victim is Tetsuo Igarashi, forty-two.{r}{p}President of a company that develops and sells computer software.”
“He used to be a programmer at another company, but about three years ago he went independent and founded his current one.{r}{p}What was it called...
or whatever, and apparently that was a huge hit.”
This is why old guys are trouble.
“A browser, you mean.{r}{p}Software for viewing web pages on the Internet.”
That brow-ser.{r}{p}It was a huge hit and the company grew fast.{r}{p}But there were plenty of problems, too.”
“First, a former colleague from the old company, Satoshi Nakajima, sued, claiming Igarashi's software was made by plagiarizing much of his own programs.”
“The trial is still ongoing, but neither side shows any sign of giving an inch, and it's become a quagmire.”
“What complicates things further is Megumi Imamura, who was Nakajima's fiancée.”
Apparently Igarashi had been hitting on her for a long time.{r}{p}Knowing she was engaged.{r}{p}And on top of that, Igarashi has a wife and child.”
“Megumi reportedly wouldn't give him the time of day, but the moment Igarashi made it big, things seem to have changed.”
“Put simply, yes.{r}{p}She secretly started seeing Igarashi.”
“But before long, Nakajima noticed something odd about her, pressed her, and everything came out. The engagement was broken off.”
“Meaning she'd have married him if it hadn't come out?{r}{P}”
But it didn't go that smoothly.{r}{p}On top of that, Igarashi seems to have lost interest in Megumi as if his earlier obsession had been a lie.”
“So she was dumped by both of them.”
“Exactly.{r}{p}Over this affair, both Nakajima and Megumi undoubtedly resented Igarashi deeply.{r}{p}And of course his wife,

Tokuko, too.{r}{p}When she learned of the mistress, she even wounded Igarashi swinging a kitchen knife.{r}{p}Fortunately the injury was minor and the police weren't called, but she's been living at her parents' with their daughter ever since.”
“Normally a woman resents the other woman, though.”
In that sense, Tokuko may be the masculine type.{r}{p}Talking with her, I didn't sense anything like anger toward Megumi.”
So those three had motives to kill Igarashi.”

“Guys like that always want to pin the blame on others.”
“These four are the prime suspects.{r}{p}Every one is suspicious, but there's no decisive proof.”

“The crime came to light on Monday.{r}{p}He was always supposed to be at work by eleven. When he hadn't shown up by past noon and wasn't answering his phone, one of his employees went to his apartment.

It wasn't locked, but the chain was on, so he was definitely inside.{r}{p}But no matter how much he called, there was no answer.{r}{p}Judging something terrible had happened, he cut the chain and went in.”
